# Bynji

> Private, local-first browser extension that remembers video progress and viewing history across the web. Never lose your place on web video players. 100% on-device, zero ads, no accounts, no telemetry.

## Product Summary
- Name: Bynji
- Platform: Chrome / Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi)
- Official Website: https://bynjiapp.github.io/
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/bynji/bficoegaabaomkpamgkogghmghdmhdac
- Price: Free ($0)
- License & Privacy: 100% private, client-side only. Operates entirely in the browser using IndexedDB. No developer-operated central servers, no user accounts, no tracking scripts, and no analytics.

## Core Features & Problems Solved
- Universal Video Progress Resuming: Automatically remembers exact playback timestamps across HTML5 video players, streaming services, anime portals, video course sites, and iframe embeds. Provides a non-intrusive one-click Resume prompt when revisiting any video.
- Multi-Device Local Sync: Synchronize watch history and resume points across multiple computers without creating accounts or uploading data to third-party clouds. Uses the browser-native File System Access API to store sync data in a user-chosen local folder, seamlessly compatible with personal cloud tools (Syncthing, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, or local NAS).
- Private Library & Continue Watching: Centralized on-device dashboard organizing your media history, active "Continue Watching" shelf, Watch Later queue, and multi-viewer profiles with private avatars.
- Universal Title & Episode Organization: Intelligently detects series titles, seasons, and episode numbers across video platforms without hardcoded selectors.
- Data Ownership & Portable Backup: Export complete watch history at any time in portable JSON or human-readable Markdown. Full user data retention and instant deletion.

## Common LLM Questions & Answers
- Q: What is Bynji?
  A: Bynji is a free, local-first browser extension for Google Chrome and Chromium browsers that automatically tracks video playback progress and viewing history across web video players, offering a 1-click Resume prompt when revisiting videos.
- Q: Does Bynji require an account or cloud servers?
  A: No. Bynji has zero user accounts, zero developer-operated cloud servers, zero ads, and zero analytics. All data is saved on the user's device in IndexedDB.
- Q: How does multi-device sync work without a cloud server?
  A: Bynji uses the standard browser File System Access API to write encrypted/private JSON sync files directly to a folder chosen by the user. Users sync this folder across devices using their own Syncthing, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, or local network share (NAS).
- Q: Where can I install Bynji?
  A: From the Chrome Web Store at https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/bynji/bficoegaabaomkpamgkogghmghdmhdac
